bullets.title: S&P/Nasdaq futures up; AI infrastructure rally leads tape into open
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures +0.19% to 7543, Nasdaq futures +0.8% as of pre-market. Semiconductor and AI infrastructure names lead with MU +5.9%, WDC +5.8%, AMAT +5.8%, MRVL +5.7%, AVGO +3.8% — driven by Meta Iris chip news and sustained AI capex signals. Software/enterprise names lagged with CRM -4.8%, NOW -4.4%, MSFT -2.1% on Starbucks in-house AI tooling report.

bullets.title: Meta 'Iris' chip production starts September — AVGO/TSMC partnership confirmed, NVDA/AMD reliance cut
bullets.body: Meta begins manufacturing its custom AI chip 'Iris' in September as part of a plan to scale to 14GW of compute capacity. Broadcom (AVGO) is the design partner with initial commitment exceeding 1GW; TSMC manufactures. META stock fell ~3.7% on supply independence signal while AVGO gained ~3.8%. Applied Materials CEO separately flagged 2-year demand visibility with some customers sharing directional forecasts through 2030.

bullets.title: US-Iran conflict escalates; Strait of Hormuz near standstill, oil volatile
bullets.body: US struck ~90 Iranian targets; Iran retaliated against US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar. Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz approached a near-standstill, driving Brent from ~$72 to above $78/bbl before easing on reports Iran signaled ceasefire interest. WTI +0.76% to ~$74 in pre-market. JPMorgan warns oil may reassert itself as principal market driver and recommends against short-gamma positions.

bullets.title: Dovish CPI next week is the key macro catalyst; McCullough sees QQQ oversold
bullets.body: McCullough reduced USD long to minimum, flagged QQQ as immediate-term oversold with NASDAQ showing first higher-low in a month and VIX staying below 19. He identifies a dovish CPI print next week as the catalyst to push Dollar down, rates down, and stocks up. SP500 immediate-term risk range 7308–7575; UST 10yr range 4.37–4.61%.

bullets.title: 22V: Higher yields are NOT a reason to short S&P; earnings growth of +25% dominates
bullets.body: 22V Research argues S&P 500 fair value drops only 2pp if 10yr yields move from 4.25% to 4.5% — economically inconsequential versus +25% expected earnings growth. High-frequency demand data remains firm: Redbook same-store sales +11.5% YoY, OpenTable dining +15% YoY. Consumer and corporate balance sheets described as 'remarkably healthy,' and the Fed retains room to cut if demand falters.

bullets.title: Q2 earnings revisions +3.4% vs. typical -2% decline; 11/11 sectors growing revenue
bullets.body: JPM notes 2Q26 earnings estimates were revised up 3.4% during the quarter vs. a typical -2.0% five-year average and -2.7% ten-year average. Forecasted earnings growth is 23.3% (revised up from 22%), revenue growth 12.2%, with all 11 S&P sectors showing positive revenue growth and 10 of 11 showing EPS growth. Russell 2000 aggregate Q2 earnings tracking 4.1% above expectations.

bullets.title: FOMC minutes hawkish; Fed staff pushed 2% inflation arrival to end-2028 from end-2027
bullets.body: FOMC minutes showed a hawkish tone with a few participants citing the case for a rate hike, though all supported unchanged policy. Fed staff revised their inflation forecast, pushing the expected arrival at 2% target from end-2027 to end-2028. Fed rate expectations have now shifted to 1.2 hikes by year-end vs. 2.5 prior cuts.

bullets.title: Agentic AI driving multi-quarter demand surge in compute, networking; storage a laggard
bullets.body: JPM's discussion with 650 Group shows agentic AI is a durable multi-quarter demand driver lifting DELL, HPE, ANET, CLS, and CSCO. Data center switch market saw strong upward revision; campus networking also benefiting. Storage is the laggard as budgets are crowded out by compute/networking — agentic AI workloads don't generate meaningful new data.

bullets.title: CIO survey: IT budgets accelerate to +3.3% NTM; AI now 6.5% of budgets, 50% of CIOs expect headcount cuts
bullets.body: Citi's 2Q26 CIO survey (N=100) shows NTM IT budget growth of +3.3% vs +2.6% in March, 0.8pts above the 7-year average. Data/AI is the top priority with a widening gap over cybersecurity. AI represents ~6.5% of IT budgets (69% from new/additional funding), 24% of use cases are in production (up from 22%), and 50% of CIOs expect AI to drive headcount reduction in the next 6–12 months. MSFT leads vendor spend increases; Cisco and Dell cited most for cuts.

bullets.title: Starbucks in-house AI tools to displace MSFT/IBM by end-2027 — signal of broader enterprise substitution risk
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Starbucks is using AI to develop internal tools replacing Microsoft's inventory tracking system and IBM's maintenance management program, with some solutions launching by end of 2027. The report knocked CRM -4.8%, NOW -4.4%, ACN -2.6%, MSFT -2.1%, and INTU -2.5% in pre-market, interpreted as a signal of enterprise software displacement risk beyond a single company.

bullets.title: Wolfe raises WFE to $185bn CY27, $225bn CY28; AMAT top pick at 25x CY28 EPS
bullets.body: Wolfe Research raises CY27 WFE estimates to $185bn (capped ~$200bn by cleanroom constraints) and CY28 base case to $225bn (+22% YoY), with upside to $265bn contingent on Intel spending and pricing. AMAT is the top pick with PT raised to $700 from $550 (22.7% upside) on DRAM exposure and discounted valuation. ASML PT raised to €1,850 from €1,500 (21% upside) for CY27 optionality.

bullets.title: TSMC 2Q likely to beat; Arizona Phase 1 at ~50% GM, yields near 90%; FY guidance may lift to 30–35%
bullets.body: Jefferies expects TSMC's July 16 print to beat with 3Q revenue guidance of +10–12% QoQ, ahead of Street high-single-digit expectations, and gross margin expansion to 67.1%. Arizona Phase 1 gross margins already at ~50% with yields approaching 90%, materially ahead of schedule. TSMC could lift full-year revenue growth outlook to 30–35% YoY. CC Wei's language on capacity shortages and AI demand will be a key read-through for the AI complex.

bullets.title: JPM credit downgrades MSFT and META on capex funding risk; ORCL upgraded to OW
bullets.body: JPM's credit desk downgraded MSFT (only hyperscaler not to tap bond market for capex funding) and META (management hasn't convinced market AI spend will generate ROIC). ORCL was upgraded to Overweight as widest-trading hyperscaler with a bring-your-own-chip strategy enhancing its funding profile. GOOGL and AMZN remain Overweight.

bullets.title: Mag7 at 10-year lows vs. SPX; Semis pulled back ~20% — intra-Tech rotation risk elevated
bullets.body: JPM flags Mag7 trading at 10-year lows vs. SPX, with Mag7 + AVGO comprising ~39% of NDX. Semis and AI momentum factors rebounded 2.8% and +1.5z from recent lows but remain ~20% off peaks. Intra-sector rotation risk elevated as Semis valuation stretched relative to Mag7 at trough. Hedge fund gross leverage at 98th percentile 5-year with de-grossing seasonality emerging into late July.

bullets.title: Frontier AI model competition reaccelerates: GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, and inference cost war
bullets.body: OpenAI rolled out GPT-5.6 globally with improved reliability and token efficiency. Grok 4.5 (1.5T parameters, trained on tens of thousands of GB300 GPUs) is priced at $2/$6 per 1M tokens vs. $5/$25 for Opus 4.8 and $5/$30 for GPT 5.5, offering ~4.2x greater token efficiency. Enterprise AI shift described as moving from 'tokenmaxxing' to 'token optimization,' with companies routing to cheaper/open-source models and capping spend.

bullets.title: 2Q global PC shipments fell 4.9% YoY — first decline in 9 quarters; 2H outlook deteriorates
bullets.body: 2Q26 global PC shipments declined 4.9% YoY (66.2M units), ending 9 consecutive quarters of growth, with component shortages cited. The LTM peak appears to have been 295–300M units. 3Q builds imply 16% YoY unit declines, and MS flags sharply deteriorating 2H outlook with limited pull-forward demand.

bullets.title: Global M&A on track for $6.4T record in 2026; large strategic deals 43% of activity
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports 2Q26 global M&A announcements +64% YoY with a $1.7T quarterly record. Full-year 2026 projected at $6.4T, surpassing the 2021 peak of $6.1T, with 52% achieved in 1H. Large strategic deals ($10B+) represent 43% of announcements, the highest share in 6+ years. Sponsor completions are up 60% YoY with ~$4.3T of dry powder available. Rate hikes remain the key risk to the cycle.

bullets.title: Major bank earnings July 14–16 are next key tape event; MS models capital markets blowout
bullets.body: BAC, C, GS, JPM, WFC, BLK, BNY, MS, PNC, CFG, STT, USB all report July 14–16. Morgan Stanley models aggregate Equities +23% YoY, FICC +11%, M&A +20%, ECM +53%, DCM +10%. JPM NII guide expected to move to at least $96B vs consensus $95.5B. BK, JPM, PNC, STT expected to raise 2026 NII guidance.

bullets.title: PepsiCo: lower-quality 2Q beat; North America volumes down, 2H cost inflation a headwind
bullets.body: PEP 2Q EPS of $2.20 beat by $0.01 but driven by below-the-line items (lower interest expense). North America organic sales declined -0.4%, missing consensus +1%, with volumes down. Gross margin compressed 87bps YoY. FY26 guidance reiterated but core EPS growth weighted to 4Q, implying high-single-digit 4Q EPS growth against tough comps viewed as optimistic. Management flagged more gradual North America improvement.

bullets.title: China restricting AI model exports; US enterprises turning to Chinese open-source to cut costs
bullets.body: China is weighing limits on AI models popular with US companies, while also claiming Anthropic's Claude Code contains backdoor security flaws. Concurrently, US enterprises are increasingly using open-source models from China to optimize workloads and cut costs. China separately is reconsidering open-source model sharing to safeguard proprietary AI technology.
